title: Architecture & Standards: Core Guidelines and ADRs
author: Evelyn Park
content:
Summary

This document codifies Redwood Inference's core architecture and engineering standards across API design, coding practices, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It also catalogs key architecture decision records (ADRs) that govern our production runtime and operational policies. The goal is to provide a single, actionable reference for engineers designing services and customers-facing features so we maintain consistency, reliability, and predictable economics.

Scope

- Applies to all teams building services that run on the Redwood platform (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Topics: API contract & compatibility, code quality, infra provisioning, deployment patterns, runtime model-serving constraints, SLOs & observability, performance targets, and ADRs.

Table of contents

1) API standards
2) Coding standards
3) Infrastructure standards
4) Model-serving standards
5) Observability & monitoring standards
6) Performance standards and SLO catalog
7) ADRs (summary)
8) Onboarding & enforcement

1) API standards

Purpose: Ensure consistent developer experience, backwards compatibility, and operational predictability for all external and internal service APIs.

Principles (short):
- Keep stable contracts: version explicitly, prefer additive changes.
- Design for idempotency for all mutating endpoints.
- Provide clear error semantics and machine-readable error codes.
- Default to low-latency responses for synchronous endpoints; offer async for long-running work.

Required conventions:
- API versioning: use path-based versions for public APIs: /v1/..., /v2/...; internal-only APIs may use semantic versioning in headers but should include a path-level major version for clarity.
- Content types: JSON for structured payloads (application/json); streaming responses use text/event-stream for SSE or chunked transfer with Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8 for plain streaming tokens.
- Pagination: cursor-based pagination preferred. Response should include: {"items": [...], "next_cursor": "<opaque>"}.
- Rate limiting headers: every public response must include: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (unix epoch).
- Error shape (machine readable):
  {
    "error": {
      "code": "string",    // short machine code, e.g. INVALID_INPUT, RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, MODEL_NOT_FOUND
      "message": "string", // human message
      "details": ["optional list of strings"]
    }
  }

HTTP status rules (examples):
- 2xx: success
- 400: client validation errors (INVALID_INPUT)
- 404: resource not found (MODEL_NOT_FOUND)
- 409: conflict / concurrent modification (CONFLICT)
- 429: rate limit / quota (RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED)
- 503: transient service unavailability (RETRYABLE)
- 500: internal server error (non-retryable by clients unless documented)

Idempotency:
- All POST endpoints that create resources must support an Idempotency-Key header and guarantee at-least-once semantics with deduplication to avoid double creation.
- For long-running inference/compilation jobs use an async create endpoint returning 202 + location header which exposes job status.

API examples (pseudo):
- Synchronous generation: POST /v1/generate -> 200 streaming tokens or 200 with final payload
- Long-running model compilation: POST /v1/models/{model_id}/compile -> 202 Location: /v1/jobs/123

Backward compatibility policy:
- Additive changes allowed without version bump.
- Removing fields or changing types requires new major version.
- Deprecation window: minimum 90 days public notice + migration guide.

2) Coding standards

Goals: readability, testability, small PRs, consistent formatting, and measurable quality gates.

Language & repo conventions:
- Primary backend languages: Go (runtime/control), Python (orchestration, SDKs), TypeScript (frontend/console).
- Repositories must include CONTRIBUTING.md with build/test instructions and a CODEOWNERS file pointing to owning teams.
- Monorepos: prefer per-service modules, clear boundaries, and dependency review for cross-service imports.

Testing & CI:
- Unit tests required: target >= 80% coverage for core logic; 100% not required but critical paths must be covered.
- Integration tests: every service must have at least one end-to-end test exercising the main API path; run in CI against a reproducible test harness.
- Performance/unit regression tests: for runtime and model-serving changes, add microbenchmarks and baseline comparisons.

Style & linters:
- Enforce linters: gofmt/golangci-lint for Go, black/ruff for Python, eslint/prettier for TypeScript.
- PR size: preferred < 400 LOC; any PR > 1000 LOC requires an architecture review.

Secrets & credential handling:
- Do not commit secrets. Use the company secrets manager (vault) and documented injected env vars.
- Local dev: use dev-only credentials and clearly documented bootstrap scripts.

3) Infrastructure standards

Provisioning & IaC:
- All cloud infra must be managed through Terraform modules stored in eng-infra; avoid handcrafted consoles changes.
- Modules required: networking (vpc/subnets), compute (node pools, GPU pools), IAM & service accounts, monitoring resources.
- Changes to shared modules require cross-team review and a staged rollout.

Networking & security:
- Zero-trust network posture in cloud: services communicate over mTLS. Service-to-service auth uses short-lived tokens issued by internal STS.
- Default deny network policy on k8s namespaces; allowlist outbound egress patterns.

Capacity & autoscaling:
- GPU capacity pools: define steady-state reserved nodes vs. burst capacity. Reserved capacity should target 70-80% utilization for cost predictability.
- Autoscaling policies: prefer horizontal scaling for frontend/routers, vertical partitioning for GPU-backed model workers.

Disaster recovery & backups:
- Control plane components must have backups with RPO <= 1 hour and RTO <= 4 hours.
- State required for inference reproducibility (model artifacts, compilation cache) must be replicated across two availability zones in a region.

4) Model-serving standards

Goal: maintain predictable latency and cost while ensuring model correctness and reproducibility.

Model packaging & compatibility:
- Models must include a manifest.json with: model_id, version, architecture, tokenizer_spec, quantization_profile, required_kernels, compatibility_matrix.
- All model artifacts are content-addressed and signed. Model upload pipeline verifies signatures and runs validation tests before marking as deployable.

Serving runtime constraints:
- Maximum synchronous sequence length (configurable per-model) should be explicitly declared; default global cap = 8k tokens for hosted deployments.
- KV-cache semantics: model workers must expose explicit APIs for warmup and cache invalidation.

Quantization & kernels:
- Quantization profiles are stored in quantization-profiles and must be listed in the model manifest. Runtime will select kernels based on profile and hardware.
- Unsupported quantizations for a hardware tier must be rejected at onboarding.

Backoff & fallbacks:
- If a requested model variant is unavailable, runtime should automatically route to a compatible fallback variant (same family, lower precision) per customer policy.
- Fallback rules must be visible in the Console and included in deploy notes.

5) Observability & monitoring standards

Metrics:
- Core metrics per service: request_count, success_count, error_count (tagged by error_code), request_latency_ms (p50/p90/p99), tokens_generated, tokens_cached_hit_count.
- Model-serving: per-model metrics: model_load_time, kv_cache_hit_rate, avg_vram_bytes, compile_time_ms.

Tracing & logs:
- Distributed tracing: use OpenTelemetry with 100% sampling for debug namespaces and adaptive sampling (default 1%) for production. Traces must include trace_id, span_id, customer_id (if applicable), model_id, and route.
- Structured logs in JSON: include service, level, timestamp, trace_id, span_id, request_id, and non-sensitive fields.

Alerting:
- Standard alert tiers: P0 (SRE on-call + paging), P1 (SRE + owner slack), P2 (email + ticket).
- Example thresholds: SLO breach alert when error_budget < 20% remaining; latency alert when p99 > target * 1.5 for > 5 minutes.

Dashboarding:
- Every production service must have a per-route dashboard showing traffic, errors, latency, and token cost breakdown. Model-serving dashboards must show per-variant throughput and GPU utilization.

6) Performance standards and SLO catalog

SLO catalog (typical defaults):
- API gateway: availability 99.95% (monthly), p99 latency <= 300ms for control plane endpoints.
- Generation endpoints (hosted API): availability 99.9%, p95 latency <= 1s for short requests (< 256 tokens), p99 latency <= 3s for short requests. For long-tail (> 1k tokens) document expected async behavior in API contract.
- Model inference node: GPU utilization target 60-80% (steady-state); per-model 99th-percentile inference time target depending on tier (e.g., small models p99 <= 100ms, large LLMs p99 <= 800ms).

Error budgets & escalation:
- Each service has a monthly error budget tied to availability SLO. When error_budget < 20% initiate an engineering review and mitigation plan. When budget exhausted, trigger rate-limiting and traffic shaping to protect critical customers.

Benchmarks & performance testing:
- All model-serving changes must include benchmark results vs. baseline (throughput, latency, memory). Benchmarks must be run on representative hardware and checked into the perf-suite repository.

Cost-awareness:
- Include token-cost per-request metrics on dashboards. New features must estimate incremental token cost and expected steady-state monthly spend in PR descriptions.

7) Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)

This section summarizes active ADRs relevant to the standards above. Each ADR is a short decision record including date, status, consequences, and owners. Full ADRs are stored in the ADRs directory and linked below.

ADR-001: Unified API Versioning (2024-06-15)\- Status: accepted\- Decision: Use path-based major versioning for public APIs and explicit deprecation windows.\- Consequences: Simplifies client routing & backward compatibility. Docs: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/adr-001-api-versioning-2024-06

ADR-007: Runtime Kernel Selection Strategy (2025-02-02)\- Status: accepted\- Decision: Runtime chooses kernels at load-time based on model architecture + sequence length profile and may recompile for hot workloads.\- Consequences: Improves steady-state throughput; added complexity in validation. Docs: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/runtime-kernel-adr-2025-02

ADR-012: Quantization-by-Profile (2025-10-13)\- Status: accepted\- Decision: Store quantization profiles alongside models and require validation at onboarding.\- Consequences: Safer rollouts, predictable perf regressions. Docs: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/adr-012-quantization-2025-10

ADR-015: Fallback Routing Policy (2026-01-05)\- Status: in_review\- Decision: Route to lower-precision compatible model variants when primary variant capacity exhausted; allow customer opt-out.

How to add an ADR:
1. Create a draft ADR in the ADRs folder with title ADR-XXX and date.
2. Include: context, decision, alternatives considered, consequences, owner, and tests.
3. Assign reviewers (SRE, Serving Runtime, Product).
4. After >2 reviewers approve, move to accepted and update this central index.

8) Onboarding & enforcement

Checklist for new services or model features:
1. Fill the architecture checklist: service purpose, API contract, expected QPS, SLO targets, and rollout plan.
2. Add CODEOWNERS and CONTRIBUTING.md.
3. Add CI tests and perf benchmark jobs.
4. Register metrics and dashboards in eng-platform.
5. Run security and compliance scan (sre/security signoff).

Enforcement & exceptions:
- Non-compliance is tracked in the architecture exceptions tracker. Exceptions require a documented mitigation plan and an expiration date.
- Critical infra changes must pass a staging -> canary -> global rollout and be accompanied by rollback playbooks.

Appendix: examples & snippets

API error example (JSON):
{
  "error": {
    "code": "MODEL_NOT_FOUND",
    "message": "Model 'redwood-rlhf-3b' not found in region us-west-2",
    "details": ["Ensure model is uploaded via the model registry and is deployable"]
  }
}

Idempotency example (curl):
curl -X POST 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 95d8f1a2-ff7a-4c3b-9c6b-2e1d9a3a4f1b" 
  -d '{"name":"test-job"}' 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/jobs

- requests per second: 200
- concurrency: 50
- max-seq-len: 512
- target-p99-ms: 1200
